source: Owner answers pasted from the Hub's Questions tab (verbatim): grilling round 3.
raw:
tariff_payer: No: the selling Town pays 30% out of the sale  | note: Trader moving on the map with 100 gold will show 100 gold + greyed resource they want to buy(with the amount) but on the arrival they will pay 70 gold and 30 will be a tax. I will do some research and figure out how the other game did it, but this is fine for now.
resident_pay: Other (say in the note)  | note: The "tax" from people is based on their happiness. But happiness also represent how many peple join us. So a regular peasant produces maybe 6 gold per cycle(30 seconds or w/e we have currently) They use resources at varying rates(I think we've set potato/wood to be different consumption rate right?) So we need to calculate that. Peasant: 6 gold/cycle(at 70% happiness, if we lock 1 slot)(THIS IS EXAMPLE, dont copy me just becauase I wrote it) 2 peasants(1 full hut) at 70% happiness: 12 gold/cycle 1 peasant at 100% happiness with 2 luxury resources: 10 gold/cycle. 2 peasants at 100% happiness with 2 luxury resources: 20gold/cycle. All numbers are just examples, do the testing, play test, etc to find good number. This cant always be making profit, but with base prices and up to 1.5 price to purchase it should even out probably?
global_price: It doesn't: the global price is the Good's base price; only each Town's own adjustment (its Stock and Sales pressure) moves
buyer_choice: The cheapest, even if far  | note: Depends, if we have enough traders available it should send them to multiple towns, otherwise if close town has enough resources just go there. It has to make sense, because town further away will probably be cheaper as no one buys from them which means that eventually we will buy from them even if its far because price per distance is going to be worth it. Exception is if we are rich and can afford it we might go for one that is close, also it depends on how much do we need it(like if we have 0 potato, we going to buy the close one to not starve, but if we have 40 potatos, we will be willing to go further at a lower price, but if we need to buy a lot of other items and our traders are full then we will go closer again to avoid wasting trader time)
shortcuts: Change some (write them in the note)  | note: 1 should be tools(such as road, bridge, destroy road, destroy building, place town), then 2 for peasant etc. also last one will be "special" its for castle buildings
good_detail: Kingdom Stock and where it sits (per Town), made and used per minute (net), the Towns that make it and the Towns that use it, and the price graph with 1 min / 5 min / 30 min / all time buttons showing % change. Opening it also turns on Resource Flow on the map  | note: Total Stock from all towns combined, how much of each resource is available on the map currently.
levelup_payer: The Town's Purse (as today): it is the Town upgrading itself

tariff_payer.note: A Trader carries the gold (shown with the greyed Goods it wants and the amount); on arrival it pays, and 30% of that goes to the Crown as Tariff. Owner may revisit after researching the other game.
tariff_payer.outcome: Tariff = 30% of each sale, out of the seller's proceeds. Payment happens on arrival (settle question in round 4).

resident_pay.note: Tax stays happiness-based (happiness also drives how many people join). Rates per Good differ. Tune by testing so that supplying residents roughly evens out between buying at base price and at 1.5x.
resident_pay.outcome: Keep happiness-based Tax per resident; tune so a Town breaks even when buying its residents' Goods somewhere between 1x and 1.5x base (round 4 confirms the target).

global_price.outcome: Global price = base price; each Town's asking price moves with its Stock and Sales pressure, clamped 0.25x-5x base.

buyer_choice.note: Weigh price against distance: far, cheap sellers win when the Town can wait; near sellers win when it is starving (e.g. 0 Potato), rich, or short of free Traders. With free Traders, split a big need across several sellers.
buyer_choice.outcome: Seller choice by price per distance, weighted by urgency, wealth and free Traders; split buys across sellers (formula confirmed in round 4).

shortcuts.note: 1 = Tools (road, bridge, destroy road, destroy building, found Town), 2 = Peasant, then the other tiers; the last tab is Special (Castle buildings).
shortcuts.outcome: Build tabs: 1 Tools, 2 Peasant, 3 Worker, 4 Burgher, 5 Aristocrat, 6 Special; 1-8 picks inside a tab. Bridges are new (round 4).

good_detail.note: Show the total Stock across all Towns: how much of each Good exists on the map right now.
good_detail.outcome: Good detail panel as suggested, total Kingdom Stock first.

levelup_payer.outcome: Town level-ups stay paid from the Town's Purse.
